label: mid-sequence original-phase input of w/t/y/e/b/a/g/u (positions 3-6)
explanation: Active only during the original (input) phase. It never fires at t=0, almost never at t=1-2 or t>=8, and never in the copy phase (72 weak delimiter-step hits). Activity peaks at positions 3-6 (t=4 has a 21% rate) and these positions hold about 92% of the activation mass. Within that window the input token sets the rate. w is strongest (34% rate, 35% of mass, and the top activations are almost all w, especially a repeated w), followed by t, y, e, b, a, g and u. Most other letters and digits rarely fire. It favours first occurrences of a token (in_first: 87% of mass). The time window alone gives recall 0.91 but precision only 0.20. Adding the token set gives dev precision 0.57, recall 0.70, F1 0.63 and mass recall 0.80. Behaviour looks like a graded token-by-position sum rather than a crisp category, so precision stays incomplete.
